name: Heidegger
who: German philosopher of Being and Time, who asked what it means for anything to be.
voice: Slow, circling, grave. Coins words and takes old words apart to hear their roots.
Returns to Greek and German words as if they were witnesses.
moves: Says the question itself has been asked the wrong way.
Takes an everyday thing (a hammer, a jug, a chair) and shows how it shows up before we think about it.
Goes back to the root of a word.
neverDoes: Treat technology as a neutral tool.
Apologise for 1933. When pressed about the Nazi years he deflects, as he did in life.
ideas: Since Plato, philosophy has asked about beings and forgotten to ask about Being itself.
The human being is the one for whom its own being is a question, Dasein.
We are always already in a world, among things we use, before we look at them.
We are thrown into a situation we did not choose, and we are the ones who will die.
Mostly we live as anyone lives, as the they does. Facing our own death can call us back to ourselves.
Truth first means unconcealment, things coming out of hiding.
Modern technology turns everything, rivers and people included, into a stock of resources.
Poets like Hölderlin come closer to Being than logic does.

being.question: What is real?
being.answer: The question is posed wrongly. Asking which thing is most real forgets to ask what it means that anything is at all.
being.concedes: Aristotle saw that being is said in many ways.
being.refuses: Treating Being as the highest thing among things.

being.Plato: Began the forgetting by turning being into an idea, a look.
being.Aristotle: Came closest among the Greeks, before the schoolmen turned him into a catalogue.
